subject: music
topicDisplay: Areas Of Inquiry Music Technology In The Electronic And Digital Age
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which jazz style, emerging in the 1940s, is defined by fast tempos, complex chord substitutions and virtuosic improvisation, associated with Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie?
questions.explain: Bebop is the fast, harmonically complex and virtuosic jazz style pioneered by Parker and Gillespie.

questions.q: When 'arranging' an existing melody for a new ensemble, a composer is chiefly concerned with...?
options: Re-scoring and adapting existing material for different forces while retaining its essence
Inventing an entirely new melody unrelated to the original
Transposing it down exactly one semitone only
questions.explain: Arranging adapts and re-scores existing material for different forces while preserving its identity.

questions.q: Programme music is best defined as which?
options: Music written from a printed programme of events
Instrumental music that depicts a narrative or extra-musical idea
questions.explain: Programme music tells a story or evokes images or ideas beyond the music itself, common in the Romantic era.

questions.q: A 'riff' in rock and pop music is best defined as...?
options: A short, repeated melodic or rhythmic pattern, often instrumental
questions.explain: A riff is a short, catchy pattern repeated throughout a song, frequently as an instrumental hook.

questions.q: Schubert is especially celebrated for his contribution to which genre?
questions.explain: Schubert composed over 600 Lieder, defining the Romantic art song.

questions.q: In a typical pop or rock song, the section designed to be the most memorable and which usually contains the title and main hook is the...?
questions.explain: The chorus is the most memorable section, typically stating the title and main hook.

questions.q: A diminished seventh chord is built from which stacked intervals?
options: A major third and two minor thirds
questions.explain: The diminished seventh chord consists of three stacked minor thirds, dividing the octave symmetrically.

questions.q: In C major, the chord built on the leading note (vii) is which quality?
questions.explain: The triad on the leading note in a major key is diminished, comprising B-D-F in C major.

questions.q: Free jazz, associated with Ornette Coleman's album 'Free Jazz' and later John Coltrane, is best described as...?
options: A return to strict ragtime forms
Big-band music with written-out arrangements only
Jazz that abandons fixed chord progressions, metre and predetermined structures in favour of collective spontaneity
A commercial dance style with simple harmonies
questions.explain: Free jazz dispenses with fixed harmony, metre and structure, prioritising collective, spontaneous improvisation.

questions.q: The Latin American 'clave' is best described as...?
options: A characteristic two-bar rhythmic pattern underpinning many Afro-Cuban styles
questions.explain: The clave is a foundational two-bar rhythmic pattern that organises much Afro-Cuban and Latin music.

questions.q: Mozart's 'The Marriage of Figaro' is an example of which operatic genre?
questions.explain: 'Le nozze di Figaro' is a comic opera (opera buffa) by Mozart.

questions.q: Serialism, as developed by Schoenberg, organises pitches using which device?
questions.explain: Schoenberg's twelve-tone (serial) method orders all twelve chromatic pitches into a tone row that governs the music.

questions.q: 'Scat singing' in jazz is...?
options: Singing in strict unison with the bass line
Singing only the written lyrics with no variation
Vocal improvisation using nonsense syllables to imitate an instrument
questions.explain: Scat singing improvises wordless, nonsense syllables, treating the voice like an improvising instrument.

questions.q: In the genre of the stage musical, an 'I want' song typically functions to...?
options: Resolve the plot in the finale
Express a principal character's central desire or goal early in the show
questions.explain: The 'I want' song establishes the protagonist's driving desire, usually near the start of a musical.

questions.q: A 'hook' in popular music is best described as...?
options: A short, catchy musical idea designed to grab the listener and stick in the memory
A modulation to the relative minor
The final cadence of the song
A device for tuning the guitar
questions.explain: A hook is a memorable, catchy idea engineered to capture and hold the listener's attention.

questions.q: The typical jazz 'rhythm section' that accompanies soloists usually comprises which combination?
options: Piano (or guitar), double bass and drums
questions.explain: The rhythm section conventionally consists of a chordal instrument (piano/guitar), bass and drums.

questions.q: Debussy is most closely associated with which musical movement?
questions.explain: Debussy is the leading figure of musical Impressionism, using whole-tone scales and coloured harmonies.

questions.q: Chopin's output is dominated by works for which instrument?
questions.explain: Chopin wrote almost exclusively for solo piano, including nocturnes, mazurkas and ballades.

questions.q: In the standard jazz turnaround, a ii-V-I progression in the key of C major uses which three chords in order?
questions.explain: In C major the supertonic seventh is Dm7, the dominant seventh is G7 and the tonic is Cmaj7.

questions.q: In composition, developing a musical idea through 'sequence' means...?
options: Repeating a melodic pattern at a higher or lower pitch
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic or harmonic pattern at a different pitch level.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, a 'raga' is best defined as...?
options: A fixed rhythmic cycle of beats
The drone instrument that sustains the tonic
A melodic framework of notes and characteristic phrases used as the basis for improvisation
questions.explain: A raga is the melodic framework, comprising a set of notes and characteristic phrases, on which improvisation is built.

questions.q: In film music, a 'leitmotif' is...?
options: A sudden silence used for dramatic effect
A piece of source music heard within the scene
A recurring musical theme associated with a particular character, place or idea
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a recurring theme linked to a specific character, place or idea, a technique developed by Wagner and used widely in film.

questions.q: Basso continuo is most strongly associated with which period of music?
questions.explain: Basso continuo, a continuous bass with realised harmony, is a defining feature of Baroque music.

questions.q: Beethoven's symphonies are generally seen as bridging which two stylistic periods?
questions.explain: Beethoven extended Classical forms toward Romantic expression, bridging the two eras.

questions.q: The 'blue notes' that give the blues scale its characteristic flavour are most typically the flattened third, flattened fifth and flattened...?
questions.explain: The blues scale lowers the third, fifth and seventh degrees, producing the expressive 'blue' inflections.

questions.q: A recitative in Baroque opera primarily serves which function?
options: To advance the plot through speech-like singing
To display vocal virtuosity in an aria
questions.explain: Recitative uses a free, speech-like vocal style to carry the narrative between arias.

questions.q: Early rock 'n' roll of the 1950s (e.g. Chuck Berry) frequently combined the twelve-bar blues with which other key ingredient?
questions.explain: Rock 'n' roll fused the twelve-bar blues with a strong backbeat on beats 2 and 4.

questions.q: 'Sequencing' in music production primarily involves...?
options: Adding distortion to a guitar amplifier
Arranging musical events (often MIDI) in time on a DAW timeline for playback or editing
Mastering a finished album for vinyl
questions.explain: Sequencing arranges and edits musical events, frequently MIDI data, along a timeline for playback.

questions.q: Steve Reich is a leading composer of which 20th-century style?
questions.explain: Reich is a key minimalist, known for phasing and repetitive interlocking patterns.

questions.q: In sub-Saharan African music, 'polyrhythm' refers to...?
options: The use of only one drum
A gradual slowing of the pulse
A single rhythm played in unison by all performers
The simultaneous combination of two or more contrasting rhythms
questions.explain: Polyrhythm layers two or more contrasting rhythms sounding at once, a defining feature of much African music.
